### Use useQuery with <script setup>

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/installation.md

All documentation examples use the <script setup> syntax. Vue 2 users can use it via the unplugin-vue2-script-setup plugin; otherwise translate to normal Composition API by moving code into setup() and returning template values.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const { isPending, isFetching, isError, data, error } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos'],
  queryFn: getTodos,
})
</script>

<template>...</template>
```

### Call useQueryClient in a Vue script setup block

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Call useQueryClient inside setup() to get the installed QueryClient, then use it to invalidate queries. Throws if called outside an injection context or if no QueryClient was installed via VueQueryPlugin.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```

--------------------------------

### Create withSetup helper for Vue 3 with VueQueryPlugin

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/guides/testing.md

Mounts a component, runs the composable in its `setup`, and installs `VueQueryPlugin` with a `QueryClient`. Returns the composable result and the wrapper.

```ts
import { defineComponent } from 'vue'
import { flushPromises, mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { QueryClient, VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

function withSetup<T>(composable: () => T, queryClient = new QueryClient()) {
  let result!: T
  const wrapper = mount(
    defineComponent({
      setup() {
        result = composable()
        return () => null
      },
    }),
    { global: { plugins: [[VueQueryPlugin, { queryClient }]] } },
  )
  return [result, wrapper] as const
}
```

--------------------------------

### setEventListener example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/interfaces/FocusManager.md

Customizes the focus event listener to use visibilitychange. The setup function registers the listener and returns a cleanup function to remove it when replaced.

```typescript
import { focusManager } from '@tanstack/query-core'

focusManager.setEventListener((handleFocus) => {
  const listener = () => handleFocus()
  // Listen to visibilitychange
  if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.addEventListener) {
    window.addEventListener('visibilitychange', listener, false)
  }

  return () => {
    // Be sure to unsubscribe if a new handler is set
    window.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', listener)
  }
})
```

### useQuery Example Using isPending and isError

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/reference/functions/useQuery.md

Same query as the status example but checks isPending and isError instead of status. Use whichever reads better.

```tsx
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/preact-query'

function Posts() {
  const { isPending, isError, data, error } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  })

  if (isPending) return 'Loading...'
  if (isError) return <span>Error: {error.message}</span>

  return (
    <ul>
      {data.map((post) => <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>)}
    </ul>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### Basic useQuery example with SolidJS

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Shows how to set up QueryClient and QueryClientProvider, then use useQuery to fetch todos and render loading, error, and success states using Solid's Switch, Match, and For components.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { Switch, Match, For } from 'solid-js'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function Example() {
  const query = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodos,
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={query.isPending}>
          <p>Loading...</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isError}>
          <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isSuccess}>
          <For each={query.data}>{(todo) => <p>{todo.title}</p>}</For>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### setOptions() example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/QueryObserver.md

Updates the observer to observe a new query by changing the queryKey and queryFn, reusing the same observer instance.

```ts
observer.setOptions({ queryKey: ['posts', 1], queryFn: () => fetchPost(1) })
// later: switch to a different query, reusing the same observer
observer.setOptions({ queryKey: ['posts', 2], queryFn: () => fetchPost(2) })
```

--------------------------------

### Basic useQuery with Solid Switch and For

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/reference/variables/createQuery.md

Fetches posts and renders loading, error, and success states using Solid's Switch and Match components. Shows background fetching indicator.

```tsx
import { For, Match, Switch } from 'solid-js'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/solid-query'

function Posts() {
  const postsQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  }))

  return (
    <Switch>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isPending}>Loading...</Match>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isError}>Error: {postsQuery.error.message}</Match>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isSuccess}>
        <ul>
          <For each={postsQuery.data}>{(post) => <li>{post.title}</li>}</For>
        </ul>
        <div>{postsQuery.isFetching ? 'Background Updating...' : ' '}</div>
      </Match>
    </Switch>
  )
}
```

### createQuery Example with isPending/isError

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/reference/functions/createQuery.md

Same query as the status example, but using the derived booleans query.isPending and query.isError for conditional rendering.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  }))
</script>

{#if query.isPending}
  Loading...
{:else if query.isError}
  <span>Error: {query.error.message}</span>
{:else}
  <ul>
    {#each query.data as post (post.id)}
      <li>{post.title}</li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
{/if}
```

--------------------------------

### useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Retrieves the QueryClient installed by VueQueryPlugin via Vue's inject. Must be called inside setup() or another function that supports an injection context. Throws if called outside an injection context or if no QueryClient was installed via VueQueryPlugin.

```APIDOC
## useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient

### Description
Retrieves the `QueryClient` installed by `VueQueryPlugin`, via Vue's `inject`. Must be called inside `setup()` or another function that supports an injection context.

### Signature
```ts
function useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient;
```

### Parameters
- **id** (`string`, optional, default `''`) - The `queryClientKey` passed to `VueQueryPlugin` — only needed when multiple `QueryClient`s are installed in the same app.

### Returns
- **QueryClient** - The installed `QueryClient`.

### Throws
If called outside an injection context, or if no `QueryClient` was installed via `VueQueryPlugin`.

### Example
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```
```

### Invalidate queries by key prefix

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/guides/query-invalidation.md

Invalidates matching queries starting with the specified queryKey prefix. In this example, both the base 'todos' and the parameterized 'todos' queries are invalidated.

```ts
import { injectQuery, QueryClient } from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'

class QueryInvalidationExample {
  readonly queryClient = inject(QueryClient)

  invalidateQueries() {
    this.queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
  }

  // Both queries below will be invalidated
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos', { page: 1 }],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
}
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider and fetch data with createQuery

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/overview.md

Configure QueryClientProvider at the project root and consume createQuery inside child components. Arguments to createQuery must be wrapped in a function to maintain reactivity in Svelte.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'
  import Example from './lib/Example.svelte'

  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
</script>

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <Example />
</QueryClientProvider>
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: () => fetchTodos(),
  }))
</script>

<div>
  {#if query.isPending}
    <p>Loading...</p>
  {:else if query.isError}
    <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
  {:else if query.isSuccess}
    {#each query.data as todo}
      <p>{todo.title}</p>
    {/each}
  {/if}
</div>
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider with useQuery and useMutation in Preact

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/quick-start.md

Creates a QueryClient and provides it to the app via QueryClientProvider. Uses useQuery to fetch todos and useMutation to add a todo, invalidating the ['todos'] query on success.

```tsx
import {
  useQuery,
  useMutation,
  useQueryClient,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/preact-query'
import { render } from 'preact'
import { getTodos, postTodo } from '../my-api'

// Create a client
const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function App() {
  return (
    // Provide the client to your App
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Todos />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}

function Todos() {
  // Access the client
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  // Queries
  const query = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: getTodos })

  // Mutations
  const mutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: postTodo,
    onSuccess: () => {
      // Invalidate and refetch
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
    },
  })

  return (
    <div>
      <ul>
        {query.data?.map((todo) => (
          <li key={todo.id}>{todo.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <button
        onClick={() => {
          mutation.mutate({
            id: Date.now(),
            title: 'Do Laundry',
          })
        }}
      >
        Add Todo
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

render(<App />, document.getElementById('root'))
```

### refetchQueries() example with active filter

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/QueryClient.md

Refetches all active queries partially matching a query key. By default (`cancelRefetch: true`), a currently running fetch is cancelled before the new one starts.

```ts
// refetch all active queries partially matching a query key:
await queryClient.refetchQueries({ queryKey: ['posts'], type: 'active' })
```

### useInfiniteQuery with initialData example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/reference/functions/useInfiniteQuery.md

Example of using useInfiniteQuery with initialData to ensure data is never undefined. The initialData provides an empty pages array and pageParams array.

```tsx
import { useInfiniteQuery } from '@tanstack/preact-query'

function Projects() {
  // `data` is never `undefined`, thanks to `initialData` — even if a refetch fails, so the
  // list stays visible alongside the error.
  const { data, isError, error } = useInfiniteQuery({
    queryKey: ['projects'],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => fetchProjects(pageParam),
    initialPageParam: 0,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextId,
    initialData: { pages: [], pageParams: [] },
  })

  return (
    <div>
      {isError ? <span>Error: {error.message}</span> : null}
      <ul>
        {data.pages.map((page) => page.projects.map((p) => <li key={p.id}>{p.name}</li>))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Set custom event listener with setEventListener

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/reference/interfaces/OnlineManager.md

Use setEventListener to provide a custom setup function that registers an event listener and calls setOnline when connectivity changes. The example uses NetInfo from @react-native-community/netinfo.

```typescript
import NetInfo from '@react-native-community/netinfo'
import { onlineManager } from '@tanstack/query-core'

onlineManager.setEventListener((setOnline) => {
  return NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => {
    setOnline(!!state.isConnected)
  })
})
```

### Prefetch on event handlers with queryClient.query

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/prefetching.md

Use queryClient.query in onMouseEnter or onFocus to start a prefetch. Set staleTime to avoid refetching fresh data; the example uses 60 seconds.

```tsx
function ShowDetailsButton() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  const prefetch = () => {
    void queryClient.query({
      queryKey: ['details'],
      queryFn: getDetailsData,
      // Prefetch only fires when data is older than the staleTime,
      // so in a case like this you definitely want to set one
      staleTime: 60 * 1000,
    }).catch(noop)
  }

  return (
    <button onMouseEnter={prefetch} onFocus={prefetch} onClick={...}>
      Show Details
    </button>
  )
}
```

### useQuery with initialData example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/reference/functions/useQuery.md

Shows how to use useQuery with initialData to ensure data is always defined. The data remains visible even if a refetch fails, and error state is handled.

```tsx
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'

function Posts() {
  // `data` is `Post[]`, never `undefined`, thanks to `initialData` — even if a refetch fails,
  // so the list stays visible alongside the error.
  const { data, isError, error } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
    initialData: [],
  })

  return (
    <div>
      {isError ? <span>Error: {error.message}</span> : null}
      <ul>
        {data.map((post) => <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>)}
      </ul>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Use mutateAsync to await mutation result

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations.md

Use mutateAsync instead of mutate to get a promise that resolves on success or throws on error, useful for composing side effects.

```tsx
const mutation = useMutation({ mutationFn: addTodo })

try {
  const todo = await mutation.mutateAsync(todo)
  console.log(todo)
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error)
} finally {
  console.log('done')
}
```

### Augment Register to set defaultError with AxiosError

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/interfaces/Register.md

Augment the installed adapter module's Register interface to override the default error type. This example uses the React adapter; augmenting @tanstack/query-core instead covers every adapter at once.

```ts
// Use the module you installed — here, the React adapter.
declare module '@tanstack/react-query' {
  interface Register {
    defaultError: AxiosError
  }
}
```

### Reset mutation error state with mutation.reset()

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations.md

Use the `reset` function to clear the `error` or `data` of a mutation request. In this form example, clicking the error heading calls `mutation.reset()` to clear the error.

```tsx
const CreateTodo = () => {
  const [title, setTitle] = useState('')
  const mutation = useMutation({ mutationFn: createTodo })

  const onCreateTodo = (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    mutation.mutate({ title })
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={onCreateTodo}>
      {mutation.error && (
        <h5 onClick={() => mutation.reset()}>{mutation.error}</h5>
      )}
      <input
        type="text"
        value={title}
        onChange={(e) => setTitle(e.target.value)}
      />
      <br />
      <button type="submit">Create Todo</button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### Add a new todo with useMutation and mutate

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations.md

Basic useMutation example that posts a new todo via axios and renders isPending, isError, and isSuccess states. Call mutate with a single variable or object to pass variables to the mutation function.

```tsx
function App() {
  const mutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: (newTodo) => {
      return axios.post('/todos', newTodo)
    },
  })

  return (
    <div>
      {mutation.isPending ? (
        'Adding todo...'
      ) : (
        <>
          {mutation.isError ? (
            <div>An error occurred: {mutation.error.message}</div>
          ) : null}

          {mutation.isSuccess ? <div>Todo added!</div> : null}

          <button
            onClick={() => {
              mutation.mutate({ id: new Date(), title: 'Do Laundry' })
            }}
          >
            Create Todo
          </button>
        </>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Configure useMutation with a scope id to serialize mutations

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations.md

Assign a `scope.id` to a mutation so that all mutations sharing that id run in serial instead of in parallel. A mutation triggered while another with the same scope is in progress starts in `isPaused: true` state, is queued, and resumes automatically.

```tsx
const mutation = useMutation({
  mutationFn: addTodo,
  scope: {
    id: 'todo',
  },
})
```

### useQuery Example Using status

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/reference/functions/useQuery.md

Fetches posts with useQuery and renders based on status: 'pending' shows loading, 'error' shows error message, otherwise renders the list. isFetching indicates background updates.

```tsx
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/preact-query'

function Posts() {
  const { status, data, error, isFetching } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  })

  if (status === 'pending') return 'Loading...'
  if (status === 'error') return <span>Error: {error.message}</span>

  return (
    <div>
      <ul>
        {data.map((post) => (
          <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <div>{isFetching ? 'Background Updating...' : ' '}</div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Using createQueryController in a Lit component

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/functions/createQueryController.md

Example of creating a query controller in a LitElement and rendering based on query state.

```ts
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { createQueryController } from '@tanstack/lit-query'

class TodosView extends LitElement {
  private readonly todos = createQueryController(this, {
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: async () => fetch('/api/todos').then((r) => r.json()),
  })

  render() {
    const query = this.todos()

    if (query.isPending) return html`Loading...`
    if (query.isError) return html`Error`

    return html`<ul>${query.data.map((todo) => html`<li>${todo.title}</li>`)}</ul>`
  }
}
```

### createInfiniteQueryController

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/functions/createInfiniteQueryController.md

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to an infinite query. The returned accessor is callable and also exposes current, refetch, fetchNextPage, fetchPreviousPage, and destroy. When options is a function, it is re-read during host updates so query keys and options can follow reactive host state. If queryClient is omitted, the controller resolves the client from the nearest connected QueryClientProvider.

```APIDOC
## createInfiniteQueryController

### Description

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to an infinite query.

### Signature

```ts
function createInfiniteQueryController<
  TQueryFnData = unknown,
  TError = Error,
  TData = InfiniteData<TQueryFnData, unknown>,
  TQueryKey extends readonly unknown[] = readonly unknown[],
  TPageParam = unknown
>(
  host: ReactiveControllerHost,
  options: Accessor<
    CreateInfiniteQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>
  >,
  queryClient?: QueryClient
): InfiniteQueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>;
```

### Type Parameters

- **TQueryFnData** = `unknown`
- **TError** = `Error`
- **TData** = `InfiniteData<TQueryFnData, unknown>`
- **TQueryKey** extends `readonly unknown[]` = `readonly unknown[]`
- **TPageParam** = `unknown`

### Parameters

- **host** (`ReactiveControllerHost`) - The Lit reactive controller host that owns the infinite query subscription.
- **options** (`Accessor<CreateInfiniteQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>>`) - Infinite query observer options, or a getter that returns options.
- **queryClient?** (`QueryClient`) - Optional explicit query client. Provide this for controllers that should not resolve a client from Lit context.

### Returns

`InfiniteQueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>` - An accessor for the latest infinite query result with page helper methods.

### Example

```ts
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { createInfiniteQueryController } from '@tanstack/lit-query'

class ProjectsView extends LitElement {
  private readonly projects = createInfiniteQueryController(this, {
    queryKey: ['projects'],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => fetchProjects(pageParam),
    initialPageParam: 0,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextCursor,
  })

  render() {
    const query = this.projects()

    return html`
      <button ?disabled=${!query.hasNextPage} @click=${() => this.projects.fetchNextPage()}>
        Load more
      </button>
    `
  }
}
```
```

### Vue example using queryOptions with reactive ref

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/queryOptions.md

Shows how to define query options with a getter that reads a ref, and pass the getter itself to useQuery so the query reacts to changes.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { queryOptions, useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const postId = ref(1)
const postOptions = queryOptions(() => ({
  queryKey: ['post', postId.value],
  queryFn: () => fetchPost(postId.value),
  initialData: { id: postId.value, title: '' },
}))

// Pass the getter itself, not `postOptions()`, so the query keeps reacting to `postId` changes.
const { data } = useQuery(postOptions)
</script>
```

### Basic useQuery with loading, error, and success states

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/reference/functions/useQuery.md

Fetches posts and renders loading, error, or success UI using Solid's Switch/Match. Shows background fetching indicator.

```tsx
import { For, Match, Switch } from 'solid-js'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/solid-query'

function Posts() {
  const postsQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  }))

  return (
    <Switch>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isPending}>Loading...</Match>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isError}>Error: {postsQuery.error.message}</Match>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isSuccess}>
        <ul>
          <For each={postsQuery.data}>{(post) => <li>{post.title}</li>}</For>
        </ul>
        <div>{postsQuery.isFetching ? 'Background Updating...' : ' '}</div>
      </Match>
    </Switch>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### Full SSR and Hydration Example with preact-render-to-string

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/guides/ssr.md

Demonstrates server-side prefetching with dehydrate, client-side hydration using HydrationBoundary, and consuming queries inside child components.

```tsx
import { renderToString } from 'preact-render-to-string'
import {
  QueryCache,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  dehydrate,
  hydrate,
  noop,
} from '@tanstack/preact-query'

function makeQueryClient() {
  return new QueryClient({
    queryCache: new QueryCache(),
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: {
        // With SSR, we usually want to set some default staleTime
        // above 0 to avoid refetching immediately on the client
        staleTime: 60 * 1000,
      },
    },
  })
}

export async function render(url) {
  // The prefetching client: only used to fetch and dehydrate
  const prefetchClient = makeQueryClient()

  await prefetchClient
    .query({
      queryKey: ['posts'],
      queryFn: getPosts,
    })
    .catch(noop)

  const dehydratedState = dehydrate(prefetchClient)

  // The render client: hydrated with the same state, used for renderToString
  const renderClient = makeQueryClient()
  hydrate(renderClient, dehydratedState)

  const appHtml = renderToString(
    <QueryClientProvider client={renderClient}>
      <App />
    </QueryClientProvider>,
  )

  // Embed both the markup and the dehydrated state in the html you send down.
  // Use a safe serializer here (see Serialization below), NOT JSON.stringify,
  // since raw JSON.stringify output can break out of the <script> tag:
  // e.g. `<div id="app">${appHtml}</div><script>window.__DEHYDRATED_STATE__ = ${serialize(dehydratedState)}</script>`
  return { appHtml, dehydratedState }
}
```

```tsx
import { hydrate as preactHydrate } from 'preact'
import { useState } from 'preact/hooks'
import {
  HydrationBoundary,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/preact-query'

function makeQueryClient() {
  return new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: {
        // With SSR, we usually want to set some default staleTime
        // above 0 to avoid refetching immediately on the client
        staleTime: 60 * 1000,
      },
    },
  })
}

function App({ dehydratedState }) {
  const [queryClient] = useState(() => makeQueryClient())

  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <HydrationBoundary state={dehydratedState}>
        <Posts />
      </HydrationBoundary>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}

// Read back and deserialize whatever you embedded on the server,
// e.g. `window.__DEHYDRATED_STATE__`
preactHydrate(
  <App dehydratedState={window.__DEHYDRATED_STATE__} />,
  document.getElementById('app'),
)
```

```tsx
function Posts() {
  // This useQuery could just as well happen in some deeper child to <App>,
  // data will be available immediately either way
  const { data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['posts'], queryFn: getPosts })

  // This query was not prefetched on the server and will not start
  // fetching until on the client, both patterns are fine to mix
  const { data: commentsData } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['posts-comments'],
    queryFn: getComments,
  })

  // ...
}
```

### Install @tanstack/solid-query with npm

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/installation.md

Installs Solid Query using npm. Solid Query is compatible with Solid v1.6+.

```sh
npm i @tanstack/solid-query
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider in Svelte

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/quick-start.md

Wrap your app with QueryClientProvider and pass a QueryClient instance to provide the query client to all components.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'
  import Example from './lib/Example.svelte'

  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
</script>

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <Example />
</QueryClientProvider>
```

--------------------------------

### createQuery Example with status Checks

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/reference/functions/createQuery.md

Basic Svelte component using createQuery to fetch posts and render based on query.status (pending, error, success).

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  }))
</script>

{#if query.status === 'pending'}
  Loading...
{:else if query.status === 'error'}
  <span>Error: {query.error.message}</span>
{:else}
  <ul>
    {#each query.data as post (post.id)}
      <li>{post.title}</li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
{/if}
```

### Create a QueryClient with defaultOptions and run a query

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/QueryClient.md

Instantiate QueryClient with default query options such as staleTime, then call queryClient.query with a queryKey and queryFn.

```ts
const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      staleTime: Infinity,
    },
  },
})

await queryClient.query({ queryKey: ['posts'], queryFn: fetchPosts })
```

Install the experimental Angular Query package using pnpm. The library is experimental and compatible with Angular v16+.

```sh
pnpm add @tanstack/angular-query-experimental
```

### Fetch data with useQuery in a component

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/packages/vue-query/README.md

Call useQuery in the setup method of a component by passing an object containing queryKey and queryFn.

```tsx
import { defineComponent } from 'vue'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

export default defineComponent({
  name: 'MyComponent',
  setup() {
    const query = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: getTodos })

    return {
      query,
    }
  },
})
```

### VueQueryPlugin.install

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/variables/VueQueryPlugin.md

Installs a QueryClient on the Vue app, making it available to every descendant component through useQueryClient. Accepts the Vue app instance and optional VueQueryPluginOptions (defaulting to an empty object). Returns void.

```APIDOC
## VueQueryPlugin.install

### Description
Installs a `QueryClient` on the Vue app, making it available to every descendant component through `useQueryClient` — the Vue equivalent of React's `QueryClientProvider`, but wired up as an app-level plugin instead of a wrapping component.

### Method
`install`

### Signature
```ts
install: (app: any, options: VueQueryPluginOptions) => void;
```

### Parameters
- **app** (`any`) - The Vue app instance.
- **options** (`VueQueryPluginOptions`) - Optional. Defaults to `{}`.

### Returns
`void`

### Example
```ts
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const app = createApp(App)
app.use(VueQueryPlugin)
```

Pass a `queryClient` you constructed yourself — useful for SSR, where you need a fresh `QueryClient` per request, or when the same instance also needs to be used outside of Vue components:
```ts
import { QueryClient, VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()
app.use(VueQueryPlugin, { queryClient })
```

Or pass `queryClientConfig` to let the plugin construct the `QueryClient` for you, with your own defaults:
```ts
app.use(VueQueryPlugin, {
  queryClientConfig: {
    defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 5 * 1000 } },
  },
})
```
```
